name: T-Deck
tagline: Handheld with keyboard, touchscreen and LoRa. All four bearers; the one you chat from.
summary: LilyGO T-Deck: ESP32-S3 (dual-core 240 MHz, 512 KB RAM, 8 MB PSRAM, 16 MB flash), 2.8" 320x240 ST7789 LCD with GT911 touch, QWERTY keyboard on its own ESP32-C3, trackball, microSD, speaker, microphone, USB-C, LiPo connector. Radios: WiFi 2.4 GHz, Bluetooth 5 with extended advertising, and an SX1262 LoRa module (868 MHz on this unit). name: T-Dongle-S3
tagline: USB stick with a tiny screen. BLE5, WiFi, ESP-NOW; the BLE-to-LAN bridge next to your router.

Runs the full xprs_app station: BLE5, LAN and ESP-NOW bearers, digipeater, cross- bearer bridge, APRS-IS iGate, HTTP API, indexer, signed OTA. name: SenseCAP Solar Node P1-Pro
tagline: Solar outdoor LoRa node, nRF52840, no WiFi. LoRa and BLE5 digipeater on a pole.
summary: Seeed SenseCAP Solar Node P1-Pro: nRF52840 (Cortex-M4F 64 MHz, 256 KB RAM, 1 MB flash + 2 MB QSPI) on a XIAO module, SX1262 LoRa (862-930 MHz), L76K GNSS, Bluetooth 5, four 18650 cells, 5 W solar panel, weatherproof case with pole bracket, RP-SMA antenna, USB-C, Grove port. No WiFi, no screen. Runs a port of the XPRS codec and bearer on the Adafruit nRF52 core: beacons, digipeats on LoRa and BLE5, bridges between the two, and dials a T-Deck's GATT channel. Built to sit outdoors unattended.

bluetooth.note: nRF52840 with SoftDevice S140 v7.3.0; one advertising set

bearers.ble5_note: Working, measured 2026-08-30 (docs/ble5-nrf52.md). tinynimble's SoftDevice port speaks to S140 v7.3.0 directly -- Bluefruit, the core's own library, is capped at 31 bytes and cannot carry an XPRS beacon -- and puts a 255-byte extended advert on the air that a T-Dongle digipeated ("via:X3WWAJ"); what it hears on BLE is bridged onto LoRa. The mesh channel over a CONNECTION is measured too (docs/ble5-gatt.md): this board dials a T-Deck serving tn_att, MTU 247, 244-byte frames both ways, hang-up and re-dial. One advertising set on this chip, so the beacon is silent while a session is up.
bearers.lora_note: Working, both directions, measured against a T-Deck on 2026-08-30: 6 of 7 beacons received there at -30 dBm SNR 12, 29 wires received here in 180 s, none corrupt and none unparsed. A beacon from this station was then digipeated by the T-Deck onto the LAN as "via:X3GSLC,X3WWAJ", so the packets are first-class on the network and not merely audible. Driven by RadioLib rather than a port of common/xprs_sx1262, which is ESP-IDF SPI throughout. SF7 / BW125 / CR4-5 / preamble 8 / CRC on, which MUST stay equal to xprslora.c or the two radios are deaf to each other.
bearers.lan_note: nRF52840 has no WiFi radio, so there is no LAN and there never will be on this board. xprs_bearer_lan is not portable here, and the LAN bearer's task is also what pumps every other bearer's re-air queue -- which is a real structural problem for a port, not just a missing feature. See the note in models/sensecap-p1-pro/README.md.
bearers.espnow_note: ESP-NOW is an Espressif WiFi protocol. No WiFi radio, no ESP-NOW.

xprs.igate_note: No IP on this board, so no APRS-IS.
xprs.api_note: No IP, no HTTP. The station talks only on the air.
xprs.indexer_note: Not ported; the 2 MB QSPI part could hold an archive, nothing writes it yet.
xprs.share_note: Nothing to serve and nothing to serve it over.
xprs.reticulum_note: xprs_bearer_rns is ESP-IDF and TCP; neither exists here.
xprs.ota_note: UF2 over USB only. No signed OTA path on this core yet.
xprs.chat_note: Nothing to type on and nothing to read it from.
xprs.note: A LoRa <-> BLE5 digipeater on a pole. xprs_codec and xprs_bearer verbatim; nothing else of common/.
